question_text: A 72-year-old patient was seen in the ER one month earlier due to accidental fall and knee trauma. Check again for bilateral lumbar pain and dark urine for a week. BACKGROUND: HTA, non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, obesity and gonarthrosis. Continue treatment with enalapril / hydrochlorothiazide 20 / 12.5 mg / day, naproxen on demand, atorvastatin 20 mg / day and metformin 850 mg / day. In the emergency analysis, the following stand out: moderate microcytic anemia, uric acid 9.5 mg / dL; CPK 45 U / L; creatinine 1.9 mg / dL; urea 75 mg / dL; Na 138 mEq / L; K 5.6 mEq / L. In urine: microhematuria ++, proteinuria - and very abundant desquamative cells. No bacteria are observed. In the previous visit to the Emergency Room 1 month ago, all the parameters were normal. An urgent ultrasound is reported as possible bilateral papillary necrosis. What could be the current picture?
